classes.objetivo: Analizar un texto de opinión identificando su tesis, su tono y dos recursos de cautela o persuasión, y citar la frase que lo demuestra.

vocabulario.es: conceder un punto, admitir una razón

ensenanza.en: My thesis is that every cycling lane in the city centre should be physically separated from traffic, not merely painted on the road.
ensenanza.es: Mi tesis es que cada carril para bicicletas del centro debería estar separado físicamente del tráfico, y no solo pintado en la calzada.
ensenanza.nota: La tesis es lo que el autor defiende y suele aparecer pronto: My thesis is… / I will argue that…

ensenanza.en: Protected routes may encourage hesitant families to cycle, but the writer presents that outcome as a likelihood rather than a promise, and she is right to hedge.
ensenanza.es: Las rutas protegidas pueden animar a familias dudosas a ir en bici, pero la autora presenta ese resultado como una probabilidad y no como una promesa, y hace bien en matizar.
ensenanza.nota: May es un recurso de cautela: hedge es suavizar una afirmación que no puedes probar del todo.

ensenanza.en: Surely no sensible parent would send a child cycling beside heavy lorries? The writer treats the answer as obvious, and that is how a rhetorical question works.
ensenanza.es: ¿Acaso algún padre sensato mandaría a un niño en bici junto a camiones pesados? La autora da la respuesta por obvia, y así funciona una pregunta retórica.
ensenanza.nota: Surely…? no espera respuesta: presenta la idea del autor como evidente y empuja al lector a estar de acuerdo.

ensenanza.en: Critics say that the scheme is too costly, so a fair writer will concede a point before she tries to make a case for the plan as a whole.
ensenanza.es: Los críticos dicen que el plan es demasiado costoso, así que un autor justo concederá un punto antes de intentar defender el plan en su conjunto.
ensenanza.nota: Conceder un punto (concede a point) no debilita la tesis: al contrario, hace que el autor suene justo.

ensenanza.en: A sweeping statement such as everybody hates cycling may sound firm, but a single exception is enough to undermine it.
ensenanza.es: Una generalización excesiva como «todo el mundo odia ir en bici» puede sonar firme, pero basta una sola excepción para debilitarla.
ensenanza.nota: Firm describe el tono; una sweeping statement (con everybody, nobody, always) es un punto débil de un texto.

ensenanza.en: Writers who deserve our trust back up their claims with evidence, whereas those who only want to persuade us often rely on emotion.
ensenanza.es: Los autores que merecen nuestra confianza respaldan sus afirmaciones con pruebas, mientras que los que solo quieren convencernos suelen apoyarse en la emoción.
ensenanza.nota: Back up = respaldar con pruebas; persuade = convencer, a menudo con emoción además de datos.

explicacion.texto: Analizar un texto de opinión es buscar tres cosas. La tesis es lo que el autor defiende y suele aparecer pronto (My thesis is…; I will argue that…). El tono es su actitud: firme, molesto, prudente, justo. Los recursos son los medios con los que convence: datos que respaldan la idea, una pregunta retórica (Surely…?), una concesión a los críticos (concede a point) y la cautela (hedge) con may, seems o to some extent. Cita siempre la frase que lo demuestra: un buen análisis no dice «es firme», dice «es firme porque…».

formula.nota: tesis: lo que el autor defiende

formula.texto: Critics say…; I concede that point.

filas.texto: Hace que el autor suene justo

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The writer persuades to the readers to support the plan.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The writer persuades readers to support the plan.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Persuade lleva un complemento directo sin preposición: persuade a alguien to + verbo.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: These plans deserve that we support them.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Calco de «merecen que los apoyemos»: deserve se usa con un sustantivo (deserve support) y no con that + oración.

situacion.contexto: Sara y Leo analizan un artículo de opinión sobre museos gratuitos antes de escribir su comentario para la clase.

dialogo.texto: What is the thesis of this article? The writer seems firm, but the tone is also fair.
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Cuál es la tesis de este artículo? La autora parece firme, pero el tono también es justo.

dialogo.texto: The thesis is that every child deserves to see the museum. She does not sound angry, because she concedes a point to the critics.
dialogo.traduccion: La tesis es que todo niño merece ver el museo. No suena molesta, porque concede un punto a los críticos.

dialogo.texto: And how does she persuade us?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Y cómo nos convence?

dialogo.texto: That is the key, I think: a rhetorical question at the end, and a figure to back up her claim.
dialogo.traduccion: Esa es la clave, creo: una pregunta retórica al final y una cifra que respalda su afirmación.

item.consigna: Según Leo, ¿por qué la autora no suena molesta?

opciones.es: Porque concede un punto a los críticos en lugar de atacarlos.
Porque evita dar cifras y solo usa preguntas retóricas.
Porque suaviza su tesis hasta que deja de defender algo.

item.feedback: Leo explica que la autora «concede un punto a los críticos»: reconocer la objeción mantiene un tono justo sin abandonar la tesis.

guiada.consigna: Lee el texto y elige cuál es la tesis de la autora.
guiada.texto: Museums should be free for everyone. I will argue that an entrance fee quietly shuts out the very people who would benefit most from a visit. Critics claim that free entry would leave galleries short of money, and I concede that point: somebody has to pay for the roof. Nevertheless, when the capital opened its main museum without charge, visits doubled within a year, and donations rose as well. Surely a country that is proud of its past should let every child see it? Free entry may not solve every problem, but the evidence suggests that it is a sound choice, and it deserves the council's attention.
opciones: Museums should charge no entrance fee, because fees keep out those who benefit most.
Museums should stay free only for children, because adults can afford the price.
Museums should raise their entrance fee, because galleries are short of money.
guiada.feedback: La tesis aparece tras «I will argue that»: una entrada de pago deja fuera a quienes más ganarían con la visita. Las otras opciones cambian el alcance o recogen la postura de los críticos.
guiada.pista: La tesis suele anunciarse con una fórmula como «I will argue that».

guiada.consigna: Elige qué función cumple esta pregunta dentro del texto.
guiada.texto: Surely a country that is proud of its past should let every child see it?
opciones: It presents the writer's view as obvious, inviting the reader to agree.
It genuinely asks readers to decide whether the evidence is convincing.
It admits that the evidence for the writer's claim is very weak.
guiada.feedback: Es una pregunta retórica: no espera respuesta ni pide al lector que valore las pruebas; da por obvia la tesis y empuja al lector a coincidir con ella.
guiada.pista: Fíjate en que nadie necesita contestar la pregunta: la respuesta ya está dada.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Los resultados podrían animar a otros municipios a probar la idea.»
guiada.texto: The figures come from one city only. The results ___ encourage other councils to try the idea, but more data would help.
guiada.feedback: Might, may o could suavizan la predicción: la autora admite que los datos de una sola ciudad no permiten asegurar el efecto.
guiada.pista: Es un verbo modal que expresa posibilidad, no certeza.

practica.consigna: Según el texto, ¿qué prueba usa la autora para respaldar su tesis?
practica.texto: Museums should be free for everyone. I will argue that an entrance fee quietly shuts out the very people who would benefit most from a visit. Critics claim that free entry would leave galleries short of money, and I concede that point: somebody has to pay for the roof. Nevertheless, when the capital opened its main museum without charge, visits doubled within a year, and donations rose as well. Surely a country that is proud of its past should let every child see it? Free entry may not solve every problem, but the evidence suggests that it is a sound choice, and it deserves the council's attention.
opciones: Visits to the capital's main museum doubled once the charge was dropped.
Donations to the capital's main museum doubled once the charge was dropped.
Most parents in the capital said they would visit more often.
practica.feedback: La prueba es un dato concreto de la capital: las visitas se duplicaron en un año sin entrada. Las donaciones solo subieron (no se duplicaron) y no hay encuesta a padres.

practica.consigna: Escucha el comentario y elige qué tono predomina.
practica.audio: I have cycled to work for twelve years, and I can tell you that paint is not safety. Last spring a van clipped me in a lane that the council proudly called safe. I am not saying that every road needs a concrete wall, and I accept that the cost is real. But surely a child on a bicycle deserves more than a white line? If councils want more people to cycle, they must first make it feel safe.
opciones: Personal and firm, though ready to accept that the cost is real.
Bitter and sarcastic, convinced that councils will never take the problem seriously.
Detached and analytical, weighing the cost of the scheme without sharing any personal story.
practica.feedback: El hablante cuenta una experiencia propia (la furgoneta), defiende su idea con firmeza y reconoce que el costo es real: firme pero dispuesto a conceder, ni amargo ni distante.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase con el recurso que usa el autor.
pares: Admittedly, the scheme is not cheap.
concesión
Visits doubled in the first year alone.
dato que respalda la tesis
It would seem that the trial has worked.
cautela al afirmar
Surely no one wants to see it close?
pregunta retórica
practica.feedback: Admittedly reconoce un punto contrario, la cifra es una prueba, it would seem limita la afirmación y surely…? da la respuesta por obvia.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué postura adopta el autor ante quienes critican el trabajo remoto?
evaluacion.texto: Remote work is not the threat that some managers imagine. Critics argue that employees who stay at home are less productive, and I admit that a few may well be. Yet the largest study on the subject, covering some ten thousand workers, found that work stayed just as good, while far fewer people quit their jobs. Surely a firm that cares about results should welcome that? I am not saying that the office is useless; teams probably benefit from meeting regularly. Even so, insisting on five days a week seems to me a habit rather than a strategy, and it may cost companies their best people.
opciones: He takes their worry seriously but thinks it is a poor reason for a fixed rule.
He rejects their worry out of hand and argues that offices no longer matter at all.
He shares their worry but believes that the evidence is still too weak to decide.
evaluacion.feedback: Admite que algunos empleados pueden rendir menos, pero concluye que eso no justifica imponer cinco días de oficina: toma en serio la objeción sin aceptarla como regla.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Con qué propósito escribe «I am not saying that the office is useless»?
evaluacion.texto: Remote work is not the threat that some managers imagine. Critics argue that employees who stay at home are less productive, and I admit that a few may well be. Yet the largest study on the subject, covering some ten thousand workers, found that work stayed just as good, while far fewer people quit their jobs. Surely a firm that cares about results should welcome that? I am not saying that the office is useless; teams probably benefit from meeting regularly. Even so, insisting on five days a week seems to me a habit rather than a strategy, and it may cost companies their best people.
opciones: To deal with an objection early and keep his argument fair.
To step back from his thesis and accept that offices are still necessary.
To reassure managers that employees will still work well from home.
evaluacion.feedback: Se adelanta a una objeción («entonces, ¿la oficina no sirve?») y limita su tesis para que siga siendo creíble; no retrocede en ella ni busca tranquilizar a los jefes sobre el rendimiento.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha el fragmento de la reunión: ¿qué da a entender la directora?
evaluacion.audio: I have read the proposal twice, and I have to say that it is detailed. However, I cannot help wondering whether the timeline is realistic, given that the team is already stretched. I would be happy to support it, provided we agree a few conditions first. Perhaps we could start with a smaller pilot and review the results in the spring?
opciones: She is ready to approve the proposal, but only after a smaller trial.
She likes the detail but thinks another team should run the project.
She backs the proposal fully and considers the timeline perfectly realistic.
evaluacion.feedback: Elogia la propuesta, duda del calendario y propone un piloto más pequeño: apoya la idea con condiciones; no pide que otro equipo la dirija ni la aprueba sin reservas.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «La autora concede un punto, pero insiste en que no hacer nada costaría más.»
evaluacion.texto: Critics say that the scheme is too expensive. The writer is happy to ___ a point, but she insists that doing nothing would cost more.
evaluacion.feedback: Concede a point es la colocación para reconocer que los críticos tienen parte de razón antes de defender la propia tesis.

repaso.consigna: Elige la descripción más exacta del tono del autor.
repaso.texto: The new bus timetable starts next week. To be honest, I am disappointed: buses will run half as often, although the town is growing. The council says that savings were necessary, and I do see the pressure it is under. Still, fewer buses will leave older residents stranded at home. Surely there is a fairer way to balance the books?
opciones: Disappointed but measured, acknowledging the council's difficulty.
Bitter and angry, blaming the council for ignoring residents.
Resigned and cold, accepting the cuts as necessary.
repaso.feedback: Se declara decepcionado, pero reconoce la presión del municipio (I do see the pressure) y pide una alternativa: tono mesurado, no rencoroso ni indiferente.

repaso.consigna: Escucha y elige cómo sostiene su tesis la hablante.
repaso.audio: In my opinion, every school should teach cooking. I know that timetables are already crowded, and I accept that kitchens are expensive to build. Yet cooking is a life skill, and it may well improve how teenagers eat. Why would we leave something so important to chance?
opciones: Cooking deserves a place in the timetable, despite the cost involved.
Teenagers already eat well, so cooking lessons would add very little.
Cooking matters, but schools should wait until proper kitchens have been built.
repaso.feedback: Acepta que el horario está lleno y que las cocinas son caras, pero mantiene que cocinar es una habilidad vital: defiende la tesis reconociendo el costo.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Los autores matizan con prudencia sus resultados.»
repaso.texto: Nobody can be certain yet. The authors carefully ___ their findings with words like suggests and appears, instead of claiming proof.
repaso.feedback: Hedge es suavizar una afirmación con expresiones de cautela (suggests, appears) cuando no hay pruebas definitivas.

classes.objetivo: Editar un borrador corrigiendo formas, registro y conectores (although, however, therefore, whereas), evitar el comma splice y justificar los cambios.

vocabulario.es: revisar una última vez, corregir pruebas
coma que une dos oraciones completas

ensenanza.en: I always leave a draft for a day before I edit it, because mistakes are much easier to spot with fresh eyes.
ensenanza.es: Siempre dejo un borrador un día antes de corregirlo, porque los errores se ven mucho mejor con ojos frescos.
ensenanza.nota: Draft y edit: primero escribes una versión y luego la editas por pasadas: formas, registro y conectores.

ensenanza.en: Although the first version was clear, it was full of slang, so I had to tone down the language before sending it to the client.
ensenanza.es: Aunque la primera versión era clara, estaba llena de jerga, así que tuve que suavizar el lenguaje antes de enviarla al cliente.
ensenanza.nota: Although + oración, oración: no lleva but. Tone down es suavizar un tono demasiado directo o coloquial.

ensenanza.en: The trial succeeded; however, the sample was small, and my first draft, with a comma instead of a semicolon before however, was a comma splice.
ensenanza.es: La prueba tuvo éxito; sin embargo, la muestra era pequeña, y mi primer borrador, con una coma en lugar de un punto y coma antes de however, era un comma splice.
ensenanza.nota: However une dos oraciones: punto y coma antes y coma después. Con una coma sola se produce un comma splice.

ensenanza.en: Fuel prices rose sharply; therefore, many households cut back, whereas wealthier families barely noticed the difference.
ensenanza.es: Los precios del combustible subieron bruscamente; por lo tanto, muchos hogares gastaron menos, mientras que las familias más ricas casi no notaron la diferencia.
ensenanza.nota: Therefore introduce la consecuencia con la misma puntuación que however; whereas contrasta dos grupos dentro de una oración.

ensenanza.en: A casual message to a colleague sounds friendly, but the same wording may seem careless in a report, so reword it carefully.
ensenanza.es: Un mensaje informal a un colega suena amistoso, pero las mismas palabras pueden parecer descuidadas en un informe, así que reformúlalo con cuidado.
ensenanza.nota: Casual describe el registro informal; reword es decir lo mismo con otras palabras, más adecuadas al lector.

ensenanza.en: When you proofread your final draft, look for every sentence fragment, because a group of words without a main verb often passes for a full sentence.
ensenanza.es: Cuando revises tu borrador final, busca cada fragmento de oración, porque un grupo de palabras sin verbo principal suele parecer una oración completa a simple vista.
ensenanza.nota: Proofread es la última lectura, centrada en errores pequeños; un sentence fragment es un trozo de frase que se presenta como si fuera una oración.

explicacion.titulo: Editar un borrador en tres pasadas
explicacion.texto: Editar es revisar un borrador en tres pasadas. Formas: concordancia, tiempos y artículos. Registro: en un texto formal quita la jerga y las contracciones y suaviza (tone down) lo demasiado coloquial. Conectores: although y whereas van dentro de la oración y no admiten but; however y therefore unen dos oraciones y piden punto y coma antes y coma después, porque una coma sola crea un comma splice. En español decimos «aunque… pero»; en inglés se elige uno solo. Anota por qué cambias cada cosa y termina leyendo en voz alta (proofread).

formula.nota: although + oración, y sin but después

formula.texto: Some like trains, whereas others like cars.
formula.nota: whereas: contraste dentro de la frase

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Although the plan is cheap, but it is not effective.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Although the plan is cheap, it is not effective.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: En español se dice «aunque… pero»; en inglés although ya contrasta y no lleva but.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The plan is cheap, however it is not effective.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The plan is cheap; however, it is not effective.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Una coma sola entre dos oraciones completas es un comma splice: necesita punto y coma antes y coma después.

situacion.contexto: Ana ayuda a Leo a corregir su borrador antes de entregarlo.

dialogo.texto: Your draft is clear, but the register is too casual. Please tone down the slang before you send it.
dialogo.traduccion: Tu borrador es claro, pero el registro es demasiado informal. Suaviza la jerga antes de enviarlo.

dialogo.texto: Which part sounds casual?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Qué parte suena informal?

dialogo.texto: You wrote that the kids are gonna love it. Also, although the plan is cheap, but it is slow: delete but.
dialogo.traduccion: Escribiste que a los niños les va a encantar. Además, «aunque es barato, pero es lento»: borra but.

dialogo.texto: Right. And can I write a comma and then however?
dialogo.traduccion: Cierto. ¿Y puedo escribir una coma y luego however?

dialogo.texto: No, that would be a comma splice. Use a semicolon, then however, then a comma.
dialogo.traduccion: No, eso sería un comma splice. Usa un punto y coma, luego however y luego una coma.

item.consigna: Según Ana, ¿cómo debe puntuarse «however» entre dos oraciones?

opciones.es: Con punto y coma antes y coma después.
Con una coma antes y ninguna después.
Sin puntuación, pegado a la frase anterior.

item.feedback: Ana corrige a Leo: una coma sola sería un comma splice; hay que usar punto y coma, however y coma.

guiada.consigna: Elige la corrección de «Although the lanes are cheap, but they are narrow».
guiada.texto: Draft report: The new cycling scheme is a total mess. Although the lanes are cheap, but they are narrow; however the council built them anyway. The kids who ride to school hate them, therefore fewer of them are cycling. Some parents like the lanes, whereas others is worried about the traffic. Honestly, the whole plan is a bit rubbish and needs fixing fast.
opciones: Although the lanes are cheap, they are narrow.
Although the lanes are cheap, however, they are narrow.
Although the lanes are cheap; they are narrow.
guiada.feedback: Although ya expresa el contraste: la segunda parte no lleva but ni however, y tampoco va separada con punto y coma.
guiada.pista: Con although no se necesita otro conector en la segunda parte.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «La muestra era pequeña; sin embargo, los autores siguen cautos.»
guiada.texto: The trial was a success. The sample was small; ___, the authors remain cautious.
guiada.feedback: However (o nevertheless) une dos oraciones con contraste: punto y coma antes y coma después.
guiada.pista: Es el conector de contraste que aparece entre dos oraciones completas.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Muchos hogares gastaron menos, mientras que otros casi no lo notaron.»
guiada.respuesta: Many households cut back whereas others barely noticed the difference
aceptadas: Whereas many households cut back others barely noticed the difference
guiada.feedback: Whereas contrasta los dos grupos dentro de la misma oración, sin punto y coma.
guiada.pista: Whereas une las dos partes sin punto y coma.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada conector con la función que cumple en la frase.
pares: Although the plan is cheap, it is slow.
concesión al inicio de la frase
The plan is cheap; however, it is slow.
contraste entre dos oraciones
Prices rose; therefore, sales fell.
consecuencia
Some like the plan, whereas others oppose it.
contraste entre dos grupos
practica.feedback: Although concede al inicio, however contrasta entre oraciones, therefore presenta el resultado y whereas opone dos grupos.

practica.consigna: Elige la versión formal y bien puntuada de la frase del borrador.
practica.texto: Draft report: The new cycling scheme is a total mess. Although the lanes are cheap, but they are narrow; however the council built them anyway. The kids who ride to school hate them, therefore fewer of them are cycling. Some parents like the lanes, whereas others is worried about the traffic. Honestly, the whole plan is a bit rubbish and needs fixing fast.
opciones: The children who cycle to school dislike the lanes; therefore, fewer of them cycle.
The kids who cycle to school dislike the lanes; therefore fewer of them cycle.
The children who cycle to school hate the lanes, therefore, fewer of them cycle.
practica.feedback: Children y dislike elevan el registro, y therefore entre dos oraciones lleva punto y coma antes y coma después.

practica.consigna: Completa el informe con el conector adecuado en cada espacio.
frases: The pilot scheme was a success; ___, several councils have copied it.
___ the evidence is encouraging, more data would help.
practica.feedback: Therefore introduce la consecuencia del éxito del piloto y although concede que los datos son alentadores sin cerrar el tema.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué da a entender la tutora sobre el borrador?
evaluacion.texto: Tutor's comment on a student essay: The argument is sound, and the evidence is well chosen. Even so, the piece reads more like a message to a friend than a report for the board; a little more care with register would go a long way.
opciones: That its content is sound, but its register is too casual for a board.
That its content is sound, but it is too long for a board to read.
That its register is right, but its evidence needs to be better organised.
evaluacion.feedback: Elogia el argumento y las pruebas, pero dice que suena a mensaje a un amigo: el contenido es bueno y falla el registro; no habla de la extensión ni de la organización de las pruebas.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Por favor, suaviza el lenguaje antes de que enviemos el segundo correo.»
evaluacion.texto: The client found our first email too direct. Please ___ down the language before we send the second one.
evaluacion.feedback: Tone down es el verbo frasal para suavizar un tono demasiado directo antes de enviar el mensaje.

evaluacion.consigna: Ordena: «Aunque el informe es breve, contiene pruebas sólidas.»
evaluacion.respuesta: Although the report is short it contains strong evidence
aceptadas: It contains strong evidence although the report is short
evaluacion.feedback: Although abre la concesión y no admite but en la segunda parte: la frase sigue con it contains.

evaluacion.consigna: Corrige el borrador (seis errores) y justifica dos cambios con «because».
evaluacion.texto: Borrador: «Dear Ms Clark, the kids in my class was very excited about the trip. Although the tickets were pricey, but we are gonna go anyway. The museum is free, however it closes early, therefore we must leave at two.» Reescríbelo en un registro formal, corrige la concordancia y los conectores y añade dos frases que justifiquen dos cambios (empieza con I changed… o I removed…).
evaluacion.respuesta: Dear Ms Clark, the children in my class were very excited about the trip. Although the tickets were expensive, we are going to go anyway. The museum is free; however, it closes early; therefore, we must leave at two. I changed kids to children because a formal letter needs a neutral register, and I removed but because although already shows the contrast.
aceptadas: Dear Ms Clark, the pupils in my class were very excited about the trip. Although the tickets were costly, we are going to go anyway. The museum is free; nevertheless, it closes early; as a result, we must leave at two. I replaced kids with pupils because a formal letter needs a neutral register, and I deleted but because although already shows the contrast.
evaluacion.feedback: Un buen borrador editado usa children, were y going to; corrige although sin but; puntúa however y therefore con punto y coma y coma, y explica dos cambios con because.

repaso.consigna: ¿Con qué propósito cambia el editor «kids» y «gonna»?
repaso.texto: Editor's note: I have replaced kids with children and gonna with going to. The findings are strong, and I do not want a casual phrase to distract the board from them.
opciones: To stop the informal wording from distracting the board from strong findings.
To correct two errors of form that would have confused the board.
To make the report sound more confident about its findings.
repaso.feedback: El editor lo aclara: los hallazgos son fuertes y no quiere que una frase informal distraiga; es un cambio de registro, no de gramática ni de tono de seguridad.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Antes de enviarlo, revisa con cuidado tu informe final.»
repaso.texto: You have finished the final draft of your report. Before you send it, please ___ it carefully, because one small mistake can spoil a good report.
repaso.feedback: Proofread es la última lectura, centrada en errores pequeños, antes de entregar el texto final.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Los resultados fueron alentadores; sin embargo, la muestra era pequeña.»
repaso.respuesta: The results were encouraging however the sample was small
aceptadas: The results were encouraging the sample however was small
repaso.feedback: However une las dos oraciones con contraste: los resultados son buenos y la muestra limita la conclusión.

classes.objetivo: Combinar la información de un audio y de un texto sobre un mismo tema, atribuir cada dato a su fuente y señalar coincidencias, diferencias y discrepancias.

vocabulario.es: en desacuerdo con, en contradicción con

ensenanza.en: According to the voicemail, the pool will reopen on Thursday, but the notice on the door gives a different day.
ensenanza.es: Según el mensaje de voz, la piscina reabrirá el jueves, pero el aviso de la puerta indica otro día.
ensenanza.nota: According to + fuente atribuye el dato a quien lo dice; no se usa con uno mismo.

ensenanza.en: When two sources differ from each other on a key detail such as the opening time, a careful reader reports the discrepancy instead of quietly choosing one version.
ensenanza.es: Cuando dos fuentes difieren entre sí en un dato clave, como la hora de apertura, un lector cuidadoso señala la discrepancia en lugar de elegir una versión sin decir nada.
ensenanza.nota: Differ from: las fuentes no coinciden. Discrepancy es el nombre de esa diferencia entre datos que deberían ser iguales.

ensenanza.en: A second account can corroborate a figure, so a detail confirmed twice is more trustworthy than one mentioned only once.
ensenanza.es: Un segundo relato puede corroborar una cifra, así que un dato confirmado dos veces es más fiable que uno mencionado una sola vez.
ensenanza.nota: Corroborate: confirmar un dato con otra fuente independiente; aumenta su fiabilidad.

ensenanza.en: Both the voicemail and the notice promise a lifeguard on every shift, but only the notice says that young children must come with an adult.
ensenanza.es: Tanto el mensaje de voz como el aviso prometen un socorrista en cada turno, pero solo el aviso dice que los niños pequeños deben venir con un adulto.
ensenanza.nota: Both + plural marca lo que coincide; only the notice señala un detalle que aporta una sola fuente.

ensenanza.en: Unlike the voicemail, which sounds apologetic, the notice is brief and formal and gives no reason for the delay.
ensenanza.es: A diferencia del mensaje de voz, que suena a disculpa, el aviso es breve y formal y no da ninguna razón del retraso.
ensenanza.nota: Unlike marca un contraste: lo que una fuente hace y la otra no (aquí, el tono y el motivo).

ensenanza.en: A reliable source makes claims that are consistent with other evidence: the notice matches the council's price list, whereas a figure at odds with that list would need checking.
ensenanza.es: Una fuente fiable hace afirmaciones coherentes con otras pruebas: el aviso coincide con la lista de precios del municipio, mientras que una cifra en contradicción con esa lista habría que comprobarla.
ensenanza.nota: Consistent with: sin contradicciones con otras fuentes; at odds with es lo contrario.

explicacion.texto: Para sintetizar un audio y un texto sobre el mismo tema, sigue tres pasos. Primero, anota lo que dice cada fuente por separado (According to the voicemail…; The notice says…). Segundo, compara dato por dato: si coinciden, usa both o consistent with; si no, differ, unlike o discrepancy. Un dato que confirman las dos fuentes se corrobora (corroborate) y es más fiable. Tercero, fíjate en lo que solo aporta una fuente. Si dos datos chocan, no elijas al azar: señala la discrepancia. Con according to cita una fuente, nunca tu opinión.

formula.nota: atribuye el dato a la fuente oral
el dato del texto: hay una discrepancia

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: According to me, the notice is wrong.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: In my opinion, the notice is wrong.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: According to se usa para citar una fuente, no una opinión propia: para ti, usa in my opinion.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Both the message and the notice says the same.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Both the message and the notice say the same thing.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Both lleva un sujeto plural, así que el verbo es say, no says.

situacion.contexto: Mia y Tom comprueban cuándo reabre la piscina del barrio comparando un mensaje de voz y un aviso.

dialogo.texto: According to the voicemail, the pool reopens on Thursday.
dialogo.traduccion: Según el mensaje de voz, la piscina reabre el jueves.

dialogo.texto: But the notice says Friday. The two sources differ, and I cannot see why.
dialogo.traduccion: Pero el aviso dice viernes. Las dos fuentes son distintas y no entiendo por qué.

dialogo.texto: Both mention a lifeguard and the same price, though, so that detail is consistent.
dialogo.traduccion: Sin embargo, las dos mencionan un socorrista y el mismo precio, así que ese dato es coherente.

dialogo.texto: Then let us report the discrepancy and ask the council which day is right.
dialogo.traduccion: Entonces señalemos la discrepancia y preguntemos al municipio qué día es el correcto.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué deciden hacer ante la diferencia de días?

opciones.es: Señalar la discrepancia y preguntar al municipio cuál es el día correcto.
Fiarse del aviso, porque un texto escrito siempre es más fiable.
Elegir el jueves del mensaje de voz por ser el día más cercano.

item.feedback: Tom propone señalar la discrepancia y preguntar al municipio; no dan por buena ninguna de las dos fuentes.

guiada.consigna: Según el aviso, ¿qué deben hacer los niños menores de diez años?
guiada.texto: NOTICE: The pool will reopen on Friday. Adults pay three dollars; children under twelve swim free. A lifeguard will be present at every session, and children under ten must come with an adult. We apologise for the delay.
opciones: They must come with an adult during the session.
They may enter alone as long as a lifeguard is present.
They must come with an adult and pay a reduced fee.
guiada.feedback: El aviso dice que los menores de diez años deben venir con un adulto; no entran solos y, al ser menores de doce, no pagan.
guiada.pista: Busca la frase que contiene «under ten».

guiada.consigna: Escucha el mensaje y elige por qué se retrasa la reapertura.
guiada.audio: Hello, this is Dana from the community pool. I am afraid that the reopening has been put back, because some repairs are taking longer than expected. Instead of Monday, we now expect to welcome swimmers on Thursday. The entry fee stays at three dollars, and there will be a lifeguard at every session. Please note that the morning lane swimming session is cancelled for the time being. Thank you for your patience, and I will call again if anything changes.
opciones: Some repairs are taking longer than expected.
Some of the lifeguards are still completing their training.
The council is waiting for next season's budget to be approved.
guiada.feedback: Dana explica que el retraso se debe a unas reparaciones que llevan más tiempo del previsto; no habla de la formación de los socorristas ni del presupuesto.
guiada.pista: Atención a la razón que sigue a «because».

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Esa discrepancia merece señalarse antes de sacar conclusiones.»
guiada.texto: Two of the sources say that the museum opens at nine. The third says ten. That ___ is worth reporting before you draw any conclusion.
guiada.feedback: Discrepancy es la diferencia entre datos que deberían coincidir; conviene señalarla en lugar de elegir una versión.
guiada.pista: Es un sustantivo: la diferencia entre dos datos que deberían ser iguales.

practica.consigna: Compara el mensaje y el aviso: ¿en qué dato difieren?
practica.audio: Hello, this is Dana from the community pool. I am afraid that the reopening has been put back, because some repairs are taking longer than expected. Instead of Monday, we now expect to welcome swimmers on Thursday. The entry fee stays at three dollars, and there will be a lifeguard at every session. Please note that the morning lane swimming session is cancelled for the time being. Thank you for your patience, and I will call again if anything changes.
practica.texto: NOTICE: The pool will reopen on Friday. Adults pay three dollars; children under twelve swim free. A lifeguard will be present at every session, and children under ten must come with an adult. We apologise for the delay.
opciones: They give different days for the reopening.
They quote different prices for adults.
They disagree about whether a lifeguard will be present.
practica.feedback: El mensaje dice jueves y el aviso viernes; el precio de los adultos es el mismo y las dos fuentes hablan del socorrista.

practica.consigna: Según las dos fuentes, ¿qué dato aporta solo el mensaje de voz?
practica.audio: Hello, this is Dana from the community pool. I am afraid that the reopening has been put back, because some repairs are taking longer than expected. Instead of Monday, we now expect to welcome swimmers on Thursday. The entry fee stays at three dollars, and there will be a lifeguard at every session. Please note that the morning lane swimming session is cancelled for the time being. Thank you for your patience, and I will call again if anything changes.
practica.texto: NOTICE: The pool will reopen on Friday. Adults pay three dollars; children under twelve swim free. A lifeguard will be present at every session, and children under ten must come with an adult. We apologise for the delay.
opciones: The morning lane session is cancelled for now.
Children under twelve swim without paying.
Young children must come with an adult.
practica.feedback: La sesión de la mañana solo aparece en el mensaje de voz; los otros dos datos pertenecen al aviso.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase con lo que expresa al comparar fuentes.
pares: The figures in the two reports do not match.
hay una contradicción entre fuentes
The website corroborates the price.
una segunda fuente confirma el dato
Only the poster mentions a café.
dato que aporta una sola fuente
Both reports give the same closing time.
coincidencia entre fuentes
practica.feedback: Do not match señala contradicción, corroborates indica confirmación, only… marca un dato exclusivo y both… la coincidencia.

evaluacion.consigna: Según el mensaje, ¿por qué cambian las fechas del curso?
evaluacion.audio: Hi, it is Marta from the studio. A quick update about the beginners course: it now starts next Monday instead of this Friday, and it will run for six weeks instead of eight. The price is unchanged at ninety euros, and all equipment is provided, so there is no need to bring your own. I am sorry for the change, but the teacher is only back from leave at the weekend.
evaluacion.texto: NOTICE: Beginners yoga course. Starts on Friday and runs for eight weeks. Fee: ninety euros. Bring your own equipment. Classes take place in the main hall. A full refund is available until two days before the first class.
opciones: The teacher will not be back from leave before the weekend.
Too few students have signed up for the original dates.
The main hall is being used for another event until Friday.
evaluacion.feedback: Marta lo explica al final: la profesora solo vuelve de su baja el fin de semana; no menciona falta de alumnos ni obras en la sala.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué se deduce del mensaje de voz sobre el aviso del curso?
evaluacion.audio: Hi, it is Marta from the studio. A quick update about the beginners course: it now starts next Monday instead of this Friday, and it will run for six weeks instead of eight. The price is unchanged at ninety euros, and all equipment is provided, so there is no need to bring your own. I am sorry for the change, but the teacher is only back from leave at the weekend.
evaluacion.texto: NOTICE: Beginners yoga course. Starts on Friday and runs for eight weeks. Fee: ninety euros. Bring your own equipment. Classes take place in the main hall. A full refund is available until two days before the first class.
opciones: That the notice is out of date on several points.
That the notice should be ignored, since the studio has replaced it entirely.
That the notice is wrong about both the fee and the refund terms.
evaluacion.feedback: El mensaje corrige el inicio, la duración y el material, pero mantiene el precio y no toca el resto: el aviso está desactualizado en varios puntos, no en todo ni hay que descartarlo.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa la tabla comparativa con datos del audio y del texto.
evaluacion.audio: Hi, it is Marta from the studio. A quick update about the beginners course: it now starts next Monday instead of this Friday, and it will run for six weeks instead of eight. The price is unchanged at ninety euros, and all equipment is provided, so there is no need to bring your own. I am sorry for the change, but the teacher is only back from leave at the weekend.
evaluacion.texto: NOTICE: Beginners yoga course. Starts on Friday and runs for eight weeks. Fee: ninety euros. Bring your own equipment. Classes take place in the main hall. A full refund is available until two days before the first class.
frases: The voicemail gives ___ weeks, whereas the notice says eight.
Both sources quote the same fee: ___ euros.
Unlike the notice, the voicemail says that equipment is ___.
evaluacion.feedback: El audio habla de seis semanas, ambos fijan noventa euros y solo el audio asegura que el material está incluido.

evaluacion.consigna: Ordena: «Según el aviso, las clases se dan en el salón principal.»
evaluacion.respuesta: According to the notice the classes take place in the main hall
aceptadas: The classes take place in the main hall according to the notice
evaluacion.feedback: According to + the notice atribuye el dato a la fuente escrita; in the main hall indica el lugar donde se dan las clases.

repaso.consigna: Compara el anuncio con el cartel: ¿en qué coinciden?
repaso.audio: Good evening. A reminder that Museum Night takes place this Saturday. Doors open at seven, one hour earlier than last year, and entry is free for everyone, although donations are welcome. Please note that the film show is now fully booked, so we cannot take any more reservations. The last visitors will be admitted at ten.
repaso.texto: POSTER: MUSEUM NIGHT, Saturday. Doors open at eight. Free entry. Film show: book online. Last entry at ten.
opciones: Entry is free and the last visitors go in at ten.
Doors open at the same time as they did last year.
The film show still has seats available for booking.
repaso.feedback: Las dos fuentes dicen entrada gratuita y última entrada a las diez; la hora de apertura y la reserva de la película sí difieren.

repaso.consigna: ¿Con qué fin menciona el anuncio la película?
repaso.audio: Good evening. A reminder that Museum Night takes place this Saturday. Doors open at seven, one hour earlier than last year, and entry is free for everyone, although donations are welcome. Please note that the film show is now fully booked, so we cannot take any more reservations. The last visitors will be admitted at ten.
repaso.texto: POSTER: MUSEUM NIGHT, Saturday. Doors open at eight. Free entry. Film show: book online. Last entry at ten.
opciones: To warn listeners that the poster's booking advice is no longer valid.
To announce a film show that is being offered for the first time this year.
To apologise for the opening time that is printed on the poster.
repaso.feedback: El cartel invita a reservar en línea, pero el anuncio avisa de que ya no quedan plazas: corrige un dato del cartel, no promociona ni se disculpa.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Como coinciden, cada una corrobora a la otra.»
repaso.texto: The voicemail and the notice both say that the fee is three dollars. Because they agree, each one ___ the other.
repaso.feedback: Corroborate es confirmar un dato con otra fuente: si dos fuentes coinciden en el precio, cada una refuerza a la otra.

classes.objetivo: Argumentar por escrito, como en una intervención de un minuto, con postura clara, concesión y cautela, y mantener la postura bajo presión ganando tiempo.

vocabulario.es: reaccionar y pensar sobre la marcha

ensenanza.en: I firmly believe that every street in the city centre should have more trees, because the shade alone makes summer afternoons bearable.
ensenanza.es: Creo firmemente que cada calle del centro debería tener más árboles, porque la sombra por sí sola hace llevaderas las tardes de verano.
ensenanza.nota: Firmly refuerza la postura: abre la intervención con una opinión clara y en primera persona.

ensenanza.en: It is true that new trees can block the view of shop windows, but that small cost is easy to justify.
ensenanza.es: Es cierto que los árboles nuevos pueden tapar la vista de las vitrinas de las tiendas, pero ese pequeño costo es fácil de justificar.
ensenanza.nota: It is true that… concede un punto contrario; block the view = tapar la vista.

ensenanza.en: To some extent, the objection is fair, which is why I would rather address it openly than hope that nobody notices it.
ensenanza.es: Hasta cierto punto, la objeción es justa, y por eso prefiero abordarla abiertamente antes que esperar a que nadie la note.
ensenanza.nota: To some extent matiza: no dices que la objeción sea del todo cierta ni del todo falsa.

ensenanza.en: When a hard question catches you off guard, you have to think on your feet, so buy time with a phrase such as let me think before you state your view.
ensenanza.es: Cuando una pregunta difícil te toma por sorpresa, tienes que pensar sobre la marcha: gana tiempo con una frase como «déjame pensarlo» antes de dar tu punto de vista.
ensenanza.nota: Think on your feet y buy time: reaccionar sin quedarte callado, con una frase que te da unos segundos.

ensenanza.en: On balance, I would say that the benefits outweigh the costs, although I admit that the evidence is not yet complete.
ensenanza.es: En conjunto, diría que los beneficios superan a los costos, aunque admito que las pruebas todavía no son completas.
ensenanza.nota: On balance resume tras sopesar ambos lados; outweigh: algo pesa más que otra cosa.

ensenanza.en: Even if my opponent makes a strong case, I still believe that the centre should close to cars on Sundays, and I stand by that view.
ensenanza.es: Aunque mi oponente presente un buen argumento, sigo creyendo que el centro debería cerrarse a los autos los domingos, y mantengo esa opinión.
ensenanza.nota: Stand by your view: mantener tu postura bajo presión, sin repetirla con otra fórmula.

explicacion.texto: En una intervención de un minuto tienes cuatro movimientos. Postura: dila con firmeza (I firmly believe…). Concesión: reconoce un punto contrario (It is true that…; Admittedly…). Matiz: suaviza lo que no puedes probar (to some extent, may, on balance). Cierre: resume en una frase (In short…). Bajo presión debes pensar sobre la marcha (think on your feet): gana tiempo (buy time) con Let me think about that y mantén tu postura (stand by your view). Evita usar dos fórmulas a la vez: no se dice I am agree ni in my opinion, for me.

formula.nota: postura: firme y en primera persona
matiz: no lo afirmas del todo

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I am agree that the benefits outweigh the costs.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: I agree that the benefits outweigh the costs.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Agree es un verbo, no un adjetivo: se dice I agree, no I am agree.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: In my opinion, for me the shade is more important.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: In my opinion, the shade is more important.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: In my opinion y for me dicen lo mismo; usar los dos a la vez es redundante.

situacion.contexto: Ana practica con Leo una intervención de un minuto para el club de debate, y Leo le hace una pregunta difícil.

dialogo.texto: I firmly believe that cities need more trees.
dialogo.traduccion: Creo firmemente que las ciudades necesitan más árboles.

dialogo.texto: Good start. Now concede a point, and then I will ask a hard question.
dialogo.traduccion: Buen comienzo. Ahora concede un punto y luego te haré una pregunta difícil.

dialogo.texto: It is true that trees cost money, but the shade saves energy. To some extent, the cost is fair.
dialogo.traduccion: Es cierto que los árboles cuestan dinero, pero la sombra ahorra energía. Hasta cierto punto, el costo es justo.

dialogo.texto: But do trees not block the view of the shops?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Pero los árboles no tapan la vista de las tiendas?

dialogo.texto: Let me think about that. On balance, I would say the benefits outweigh the costs, and I stand by that view.
dialogo.traduccion: Déjame pensarlo. En conjunto, diría que los beneficios superan a los costos, y mantengo esa opinión.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿cómo responde Ana a la pregunta difícil de Leo?

opciones.es: Gana tiempo con una frase y mantiene su postura con matiz.
Cambia de postura y da la razón a Leo sin discutir.
Evita responder y cambia de tema para no perder tiempo.

item.feedback: Ana empieza con «Let me think about that» (gana tiempo) y después mantiene su postura con on balance y I stand by that view.

guiada.consigna: Elige la apertura que expresa una postura clara y firme.
guiada.texto: Topic for your one-minute talk: should the local cinema stay open later at weekends?
opciones: I firmly believe that the cinema should stay open until midnight at weekends.
Some people say that a later closing time may help, but I really could not say.
I have read that several cinemas have tried staying open until midnight.
guiada.feedback: I firmly believe… declara la postura con claridad; las otras opciones dudan o solo citan lo que dicen otros.
guiada.pista: Busca la frase en primera persona con un adverbio que refuerza la opinión.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «En conjunto, diría que los beneficios superan a los riesgos.»
guiada.texto: Critics say that a car-free centre would hurt shops. On ___, I would say that the benefits outweigh the risks, although the evidence is still limited.
guiada.feedback: On balance introduce una conclusión tras sopesar los dos lados del argumento, con la cautela de reconocer que faltan datos.
guiada.pista: Es el sustantivo de la balanza: conclusión tras sopesar los dos lados.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Mantengo mi opinión de que los beneficios superan los costos.»
guiada.respuesta: I stand by my view that the benefits outweigh the costs
guiada.feedback: Stand by my view es mantener la opinión propia; outweigh expresa que los beneficios pesan más que los costos.
guiada.pista: Empieza con el sujeto y el verbo frasal de mantener una opinión.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué función cumple «To some extent, those worries are fair».
practica.audio: I firmly believe that our town should close its main square to cars on Sundays. It is true that some drivers will be annoyed, and I accept that a few cafes may lose customers at first. To some extent, those worries are fair. Nevertheless, the evidence from other towns suggests that more people walk into the centre, and surely a quiet square is worth a little trouble? On balance, the benefits outweigh the costs.
opciones: It gives the critics a small point before the speaker carries on.
It cancels the speaker's proposal until the critics' worries are settled.
It introduces a statistic that shows the speaker's proposal will work.
practica.feedback: To some extent concede un punto pequeño a quienes se preocupan por los cafés, pero la hablante sigue con Nevertheless y mantiene su postura: no retira la propuesta.

practica.consigna: Elige la frase que gana tiempo sin parecer evasiva.
practica.texto: At a debate, a classmate asks you a question that you did not expect, and you need a moment to think.
opciones: That is a fair challenge; let me gather my thoughts before I answer it properly.
That is a fair challenge, so I will move on to the next topic, if you do not mind.
That is a fair challenge, but honestly I have never thought about it before.
practica.feedback: Reconoce la pregunta y pide un momento para ordenar ideas, pero promete responder; las otras opciones esquivan la pregunta o admiten no tener respuesta.

practica.consigna: Completa: «Aun así, mantengo mi opinión de que el plan ayudará.»
practica.texto: Some of my friends disagree with me, and I respect that. Even so, I ___ by my view that the plan will help.
practica.feedback: Stand by your view significa mantener tu opinión aunque otros discrepen, sin dejar de respetarlos.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué elemento falta en esta intervención para cumplir la tarea?
evaluacion.texto: I firmly believe that schools should start later. Teenagers need more sleep, and tired students cannot concentrate. Surely nobody wants exhausted children in the first lesson? In short, a later start may well improve results and make mornings calmer for everybody.
opciones: A concession that recognises the strongest objection to the plan.
A clear position stated at the start of the talk.
A closing sentence that sums up the speaker's view.
evaluacion.feedback: La intervención tiene postura (I firmly believe), cautela (may well) y cierre (In short), pero nunca reconoce un punto contrario: falta la concesión.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha la respuesta: ¿qué hace la hablante con la pregunta?
evaluacion.audio: Hmm, that is a fair question. Give me a second. Well, to some extent I agree with you, but I would say that the real issue is cost. If we ignore that, the plan will not work, whatever else is good about it.
opciones: She agrees only in part and moves the discussion towards cost.
She agrees completely and adds a further reason to support the plan.
She disagrees politely and suggests that cost is not a real issue.
evaluacion.feedback: Gana tiempo («Give me a second»), concede hasta cierto punto y desplaza el debate hacia el costo: acuerdo parcial, no total ni rechazo.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «En conjunto, las ventajas superan con mucho a las desventajas.»
evaluacion.texto: The plan has some real drawbacks. On the whole, however, the advantages far ___ the disadvantages.
evaluacion.feedback: Outweigh es el verbo para decir que un lado de la balanza pesa más que el otro: aquí, las ventajas pesan más que los inconvenientes.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe tu intervención de un minuto: postura, concesión y cautela.
evaluacion.texto: Tema: ¿debería ser gratuito el transporte público en las ciudades? Escribe unas 200 palabras (lo que dirías en un minuto): defiende una postura con claridad, concede un punto contrario, usa cautela (to some extent, may, perhaps, it seems, on balance) y cierra con In short o To sum up.
evaluacion.respuesta: I firmly believe that public transport in our city should be free for everyone. First, it would help families who spend a large part of their income on travel, and it would encourage more people to leave their cars at home. As a result, the streets would be quieter, the air would be cleaner and the centre would be safer for children. It is true that free buses would cost the council a great deal of money, and some critics argue that the service might become crowded. To some extent, I share that worry. However, it seems that the money could come from parking fees and from the money that we already spend on roads. Perhaps we could begin with a one-year trial and review the results carefully. On the other hand, nobody can promise that every passenger would leave a car at home. Even so, on balance, I would say that the benefits outweigh the costs, and I stand by that view. In short, free public transport would make our city fairer, cleaner and calmer.
aceptadas: My position is clear: public transport should cost nothing for residents. Admittedly, it is not a cheap idea, and the council would have to find a large sum every year. Even so, I am convinced that the money would be well spent. Cheaper travel would help students, workers and older people who cannot afford a car, and it may also reduce traffic in the centre. Some say that buses would become crowded, and I agree that the service would need more vehicles. Perhaps the city could add a few routes at busy hours and review the plan after twelve months. It seems to me that nobody can be certain of the result before trying. However, doing nothing is also a choice, and it has costs of its own: noise, pollution and long delays. To sum up, free transport is a fair and sensible idea, and on balance I think it is worth a try.
evaluacion.feedback: Una buena intervención abre con una postura firme, concede un punto contrario, matiza con cautela, sopesa el otro lado y cierra con un resumen.

repaso.consigna: Escucha el comentario y elige qué actitud transmite la hablante.
repaso.audio: I understand why some neighbours dislike the idea, and to some extent I share their concern about noise. All the same, I firmly believe that the new market would bring life to the street. Let us try it for three months, and if it does not work, I will be the first to say so.
opciones: Firm but open-minded, willing to test her idea and accept the result.
Stubborn, determined to go ahead whatever the neighbours may think of it.
Doubtful, ready to drop the idea because of the noise it would cause.
repaso.feedback: Reconoce la preocupación de los vecinos, mantiene su idea con firmeza y propone una prueba de tres meses: firme pero abierta a rectificar.

repaso.consigna: Elige la respuesta que gana tiempo y mantiene la postura con matiz.
repaso.texto: At the end of your talk on free museums, a listener asks: Who would pay for all this?
opciones: Good question; let me think. The council would pay part of it, and I stand by my view.
Good question, but I have already answered it earlier, so I will not repeat myself now.
Good question; I suppose you may be right, so perhaps my whole argument is wrong after all.
repaso.feedback: Gana tiempo, da una respuesta parcial y mantiene su postura con matiz; las otras opciones cortan la conversación o abandonan la tesis.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Decir «Let me think» puede ayudarte a ganar tiempo.»
repaso.texto: Nobody expected the question, and the speaker's mind went blank for a moment. Saying let me think can help her ___ time until an answer comes.
repaso.feedback: Buy time es la colocación para ganar unos segundos con una frase de transición mientras ordenas la respuesta.

classes.objetivo: Resolver un caso final de entrada C1: interpretar lo implícito de un mensaje, responder con tacto y defender una postura con matiz.

vocabulario.es: andar con pies de plomo, mantener un equilibrio delicado

ensenanza.en: When I read the landlord's message twice, I began to interpret the polite wording as a gentle complaint about the state of the garden.
ensenanza.es: Cuando leí dos veces el mensaje de la casera, empecé a interpretar su cortés redacción como una queja suave sobre el estado del jardín.
ensenanza.nota: Interpretar es el primer paso: tono, registro y lo que se sugiere sin decirlo.

ensenanza.en: Her email never said that I was late, but it implied that I should have arrived earlier, so I had to read between the lines.
ensenanza.es: Su correo nunca decía que yo llegaba tarde, pero daba a entender que debí llegar antes, así que tuve que leer entre líneas.
ensenanza.nota: Imply + that + oración: sugerir sin decirlo; no se dice implied me. Read between the lines: captar lo no dicho.

ensenanza.en: I have to tread a fine line here: I admit that the landlord's costs have risen, although I take issue with the claim that the rent rise is unavoidable.
ensenanza.es: Tengo que andar con pies de plomo: admito que los costos del casero han subido, aunque discrepo de la afirmación de que la subida del alquiler sea inevitable.
ensenanza.nota: Tread a fine line: equilibrio delicado entre firmeza y cortesía; admit reconoce un punto débil, y take issue with discrepa con educación.

ensenanza.en: Thank you for your generous offer; nevertheless, I must decline, because the dates clash with another commitment I cannot move.
ensenanza.es: Gracias por tu generosa oferta; sin embargo, debo rechazarla, porque las fechas coinciden con otro compromiso que no puedo mover.
ensenanza.nota: Reconoce primero y rechaza después con decline y nevertheless: tacto y claridad.

ensenanza.en: To hold your ground without sounding rude, acknowledge the other person's concern first and only then state your position clearly.
ensenanza.es: Para mantenerte firme sin parecer grosero, reconoce primero la preocupación de la otra persona y solo después expón tu postura con claridad.
ensenanza.nota: Hold your ground: no ceder en lo esencial; el orden (reconocer, luego postura) protege la relación.

ensenanza.en: Writing with tact means you strike a balance between honesty and courtesy, and a little nuance shows that you have weighed both sides.
ensenanza.es: Escribir con tacto significa encontrar un equilibrio entre la sinceridad y la cortesía, y un poco de matiz demuestra que has sopesado ambas partes.
ensenanza.nota: Strike a balance: encontrar el punto medio; nuance es la mezcla de concesión, cautela y firmeza.

explicacion.titulo: El caso final: interpretar, responder, defender
explicacion.texto: Este cierre junta todo el nivel en un caso de tres pasos. Interpretar: lee el mensaje buscando tono, registro y lo implícito (read between the lines; her email implied that…). Responder con tacto: agradece, reconoce un punto (I understand…; I admit…) y rechaza o propón con suavidad (I'm afraid…; nevertheless, I must decline). Defender tu postura con matiz: firmeza (I firmly believe…), concesión y cautela (may, to some extent), buscando el equilibrio (strike a balance, tread a fine line) entre ser sincero y ser cortés, sin ceder en lo esencial (hold your ground). Cierra con un acuerdo concreto (Could we agree to…?).

formula.texto: Her email implied that I was late.
formula.nota: interpretar: lo implícito, con implied that

formula.texto: I understand your concern; nevertheless, I must decline.
I firmly believe it is fair, although I admit…

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I am not agree with your plan, you are wrong.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: I see your point; nevertheless, I see it differently.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Agree es un verbo (I don't agree), y decir «you are wrong» es brusco: reconoce el punto y discrepa con tacto.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Her email implied me that I was late.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Her email implied that I was late.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Calco de «me dio a entender que»: imply no lleva pronombre de persona; se dice implied that + oración.

situacion.contexto: Tom recibe un mensaje de su casera y le pide ayuda a Mia para interpretarlo y contestar.

dialogo.texto: My landlord wrote: It would be lovely if the garden were tidy before Sunday.
dialogo.traduccion: Mi casera escribió: «Sería estupendo que el jardín estuviera ordenado antes del domingo.»

dialogo.texto: That is polite, but read between the lines: she implies that the garden is a mess.
dialogo.traduccion: Es educado, pero lee entre líneas: da a entender que el jardín está hecho un desastre.

dialogo.texto: I think so too. But my neighbour uses the garden too, so I take issue with the idea that it is all my fault.
dialogo.traduccion: Yo también lo creo. Pero mi vecino también usa el jardín, así que no estoy de acuerdo con que sea todo culpa mía.

dialogo.texto: Then thank her first and say, with tact, that you will tidy only your part.
dialogo.traduccion: Entonces dale las gracias primero y di, con tacto, que solo ordenarás tu parte.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué recomienda Mia para la respuesta de Tom?

opciones.es: Agradecer primero y aclarar con tacto que solo ordenará su parte.
Ignorar el mensaje porque es demasiado educado para ser una queja.
Responder con sarcasmo para marcar su postura desde el principio.

item.feedback: Mia dice «thank her first» y aclarar «with tact» que solo ordenará su parte: respuesta cortés que mantiene una postura.

guiada.consigna: Interpreta el mensaje: ¿qué da a entender el compañero?
guiada.texto: Note from a colleague: I see that the shared calendar has been left blank again this week. I am sure that everybody has had a lot on.
opciones: He politely implies that somebody forgot to update the calendar.
He sincerely believes that everybody has been too busy, and sees no problem.
He is asking colleagues to empty the calendar so that it can be updated.
guiada.feedback: No acusa a nadie, pero «left blank again» y «I am sure everybody has had a lot on» sugieren con cortesía que alguien olvidó rellenarlo; tomarlo al pie de la letra sería no leer entre líneas.
guiada.pista: Fíjate en lo que dice sobre el calendario sin pedirlo directamente.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Nunca dice que está molesta, pero hay que leer entre líneas.»
guiada.texto: Your manager's email never says that she is unhappy with you, but you have to read ___ the lines.
guiada.feedback: Read between the lines es captar lo que un mensaje sugiere sin decirlo de forma explícita.
guiada.pista: La preposición significa «entre» y aparece en la enseñanza.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Gracias por la oferta; sin embargo, debo rechazarla.»
guiada.respuesta: Thank you for the offer nevertheless I must decline it
guiada.feedback: Se agradece primero, y nevertheless introduce el rechazo con decline: cortés pero claro.
guiada.pista: Empieza agradeciendo y deja nevertheless para el rechazo.

practica.consigna: Escucha el mensaje: ¿qué quiere decir en realidad Elena?
practica.audio: Hi, it is Elena from upstairs. I hope you do not mind me mentioning this, but I could not help noticing that the recycling bins were still on the pavement on Friday morning. I am sure it was just a mistake, and I know how busy this month has been for everybody. It is only that the pavement was blocked for a while. Anyway, thanks so much, and I hope you have a lovely weekend.
opciones: She is politely complaining and hopes it will not happen again.
She is sincerely reassuring him that the bins were not a problem at all.
She is warning him that the council will fine everyone for blocked pavements.
practica.feedback: Elena suaviza la queja («I am sure it was just a mistake») pero deja claro que los contenedores bloquearon la acera: es una queja cortés, no una tranquilización.

practica.consigna: Elige la respuesta que agradece, reconoce sus costos y defiende tu postura.
practica.texto: Your landlord writes: From next month the rent will rise, as our costs have gone up. I trust that this will not be a problem.
opciones: Thank you for explaining. I understand your costs; nevertheless, could we discuss a smaller rise?
Thank you for explaining. I understand your costs, so I accept the rise without any question.
Thank you for explaining, but the rise is unfair, and I expect you to cancel it.
practica.feedback: Agradece, reconoce el problema del casero y propone hablar: es cortés y defiende su postura; una respuesta cede sin más y la otra exige sin matiz.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase con su función en la respuesta final.
pares: Thank you for letting me know.
reconocer el mensaje
I am afraid I must decline.
rechazar con tacto
On balance, I think the plan is fair.
postura con matiz
Could we agree to meet on Friday?
cerrar con un acuerdo concreto
practica.feedback: Thank you reconoce, I am afraid I must decline rechaza con suavidad, on balance matiza la postura y Could we agree…? propone un acuerdo.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué espera realmente Helen de Tom?
evaluacion.texto: Dear Tom, thank you for your report, which was, as always, detailed. I did wonder whether the section on costs might benefit from a little more explanation, and perhaps a second pair of eyes before it goes to the board on Thursday. No rush, of course. Kind regards, Helen.
opciones: That he revises the cost section before the board meets on Thursday.
That he leaves the report as it is, because it was already detailed.
That he postpones sending the report until after the board meeting.
evaluacion.feedback: «I did wonder whether the section on costs might benefit from more explanation» es una petición cortés: quiere que lo revise antes del jueves.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué postura defiende la hablante.
evaluacion.audio: I admit that the plan is not perfect, and I can see why some residents are anxious. Even so, I firmly believe that it is the fairest option we have. A smaller scheme would hardly make a difference, whereas doing nothing would cost us far more in the long run.
opciones: She defends the plan while admitting that it has some flaws.
She rejects the plan completely and proposes a smaller scheme.
She is unsure about the plan and asks for another proposal.
evaluacion.feedback: Admite que el plan no es perfecto, pero mantiene con firmeza que es la opción más justa: postura defendida con matiz.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «No quiero ser grosero, pero debo discrepar de las cifras de tu informe.»
evaluacion.texto: I do not want to sound rude, but I must ___ issue with the figures in your report.
evaluacion.feedback: Take issue with es la colocación para discrepar de algo con educación pero con claridad.

evaluacion.consigna: Responde al mensaje con tacto y defiende tu postura con matiz.
evaluacion.texto: Caso final. Tu compañero de casa escribe: «Some of us seem to do all the cleaning while others are always out.» Escribe entre 160 y 270 palabras: interpreta lo que implica, agradece, reconoce un punto, defiende tu postura con cautela (tu horario de trabajo te deja poco tiempo) y propón un plan (un calendario) con un acuerdo concreto.
evaluacion.respuesta: Hi Sam, thank you for your message. I think you are saying that the cleaning is not shared fairly, and I understand why you feel that way. It is true that I have been out a lot this month, and I admit that some weeks you have done more than your part. However, I firmly believe that the problem is partly my work schedule, because I finish late on most days and I am often too tired to clean. To some extent, that may explain why the flat looks worse than before. I am afraid I cannot clean every day, but I would like to find a fair solution. I also want to say that I appreciate how much you have done, and I do not want this to become a bigger problem between us. Could we agree to make a weekly calendar? I could take the kitchen on Saturdays, and you could choose another task. What do you think? Let us review the plan in two weeks. Thanks again for being honest with me.
aceptadas: Hello Sam, thanks for telling me how you feel. Your message suggests that I am not doing enough, and I can see why you are upset. Admittedly, I have not cleaned much lately, and I am sorry about that. Still, my new job means that I work late most evenings, so perhaps the real problem is time, not effort. I am not sure that a strict rule would help, but a simple calendar might. What if we share the tasks by day, and I take the bathroom and the kitchen at weekends? We could try it for a month and then check whether it works for both of us. I would also like us to be more open with each other, because small problems grow when nobody talks about them. I hope that sounds fair, and thank you for being patient with me. Let us talk about it over dinner this week, and then we can write the calendar together.
evaluacion.feedback: Una buena respuesta interpreta lo implícito, agradece, concede un punto, defiende la postura con cautela y propone un plan concreto.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Entiendo tu preocupación; sin embargo, mantengo mi postura.»
repaso.respuesta: I understand your concern nevertheless I keep my position
repaso.feedback: Se reconoce primero la preocupación y nevertheless marca el contraste: se mantiene la postura sin romper la cortesía.

repaso.consigna: Elige la respuesta con más tacto y matiz a la propuesta.
repaso.texto: Your manager proposes moving the weekly meeting to eight in the morning. Several colleagues have small children, and you think the plan is unfair, but you want to stay on good terms.
opciones: Thank you for the idea. I admit it helps some people, but eight is hard for parents.
I take issue with this plan. Eight is far too early, and I am sure that everybody agrees with me.
Thanks, eight is fine. I will tell the others, even though I think that it is quite unfair.
repaso.feedback: Agradece, admite un punto a favor y expone el problema con matiz; las otras respuestas confrontan o ceden en contra de su opinión.

repaso.consigna: Escucha el mensaje y elige cómo suena la hablante.
repaso.audio: Oh, brilliant. Another meeting at eight in the morning. Just what we needed after the week we have had. I am sure everybody will be thrilled to give up their Friday evening too.
opciones: Sarcastic: she is unhappy about the plan and says the opposite.
Enthusiastic: she is pleased to have one more meeting this week.
Neutral: she is reporting the new time without any opinion about it.
repaso.feedback: «Oh, brilliant… Just what we needed» es sarcasmo: dice lo contrario de lo que siente, porque no quiere otra reunión a las ocho; no es entusiasmo ni un aviso neutral.

notes: Claves verificadas contra texto/audio en las 5 clases; distractores reescritos como casi-aciertos (lectura literal, postura invertida, cierto pero no dicho) en C96-C100.
C98: aviso del curso sin el día 'Tuesday' (contradecía el inicio el viernes); ordenar adaptado; aceptadas ampliadas (discrepancy/corroborates).
Rúbricas de C97, C99 y C100 pasan a grupos de frases (sin palabras sueltas como because/may/schedule); modelos y aceptadas las superan.

Español neutro: enfadado/hueco/escaparates/coches/pilla/piso sustituidos. Colocaciones C1 de las entradas nuevas conservadas; C98 tabla comparativa aproximada con completar multiparte sobre audio + aviso (aceptado).

P2 pendiente: C98 usa el escenario de la piscina tanto en la tabla de enseñanza como en la práctica (no en evaluación); C100 pide 160-270 palabras frente a 220-270 del mapa (modelo de 175 ≥ 70 % del mínimo).
